runtimeRule: A class requires a live register row, a real video, and a current admitted class learning record.

records.learningObjective: Distinguish an AI app from the model and other services it can use, trace what becomes working context, and choose what needs verification.
records.prerequisite: No prior AI knowledge; learner can open one conversational AI product.
records.mentalModel: The app coordinates instructions, conversation context and optional capabilities such as files, search or other tools; a model processes the supplied context and produces or helps select the next output or action.
adjacentDistinctions: a model capability versus a product feature or account entitlement
misconceptions: The app and the model are the same thing.
Conversational AI never searches or uses tools.
Anything an assistant says came from a verified source.
A new chat always means the product has no other memory or connected data.

modality.narration: Build the app-model-tools-context distinction in that order and state uncertainty before the demonstration.
modality.images: Use a labelled layer diagram and real, date-stamped interface captures; every image must match the narration at that moment.
modality.animation: Animate only the flow of a request, optional tool result and response. Do not use decorative character motion as a substitute for the mechanism.
modality.demonstration: Run one task first without search and then with visible search/citations, naming what changed and what still requires checking.
modality.captions: Caption the final approved narration verbatim and identify meaningful interface states without relying on colour alone.

analogy.text: Think of the app as a studio, the model as one performer, and tools as equipment the studio may make available.
analogy.limit: A model is not a person, and product orchestration is not literally a studio; use the analogy only to separate layers.

uncertainty: Product features, defaults, model names and account entitlements change.
Vendors use overlapping terms for models, assistants, apps, tools, memory and connectors.

records.objective: Check whether the learner can apply the app-model-tools-context distinction and choose an appropriate verification action.

questions.prompt: You upload a PDF in an AI app and ask for a summary. Which description is most accurate?
options: The app supplies the file and instructions as working context for a model to process.
The model permanently learns the whole PDF for every future user.
Uploading proves every statement in the PDF is true.
questions.answer: The app supplies the file and instructions as working context for a model to process.
questions.explanation: The product handles the file and passes usable information to the model. That does not make the file true or permanently retrain the model.
questions.misconception: File upload means permanent training or automatic verification.
questions.reviewAction: Return to the request-flow diagram and name the app, context and model layers.

questions.prompt: An answer includes clickable web citations. What changed?
options: The product used a search or retrieval capability and supplied results to the answering flow.
The model became incapable of generating text.
Every cited claim is now guaranteed correct.
questions.answer: The product used a search or retrieval capability and supplied results to the answering flow.
questions.explanation: Search can add current source material, but the learner must still inspect whether each source supports the claim.
questions.reviewAction: Open one citation and compare the source with the sentence it is meant to support.

questions.prompt: Two products use similarly named models but show different buttons and limits. Why can that happen?
options: Product features, connected tools and account entitlements can differ from the underlying model.
A model name determines every part of an app.
One of the products must be fake.
questions.answer: Product features, connected tools and account entitlements can differ from the underlying model.
questions.explanation: The model is one layer. The app controls interface, tool access, policies, limits and account features.
questions.misconception: Model capability and product availability are identical.
questions.reviewAction: Name one feature controlled by the app rather than the model alone.

questions.prompt: A new chat remembers a preference. What is the safest conclusion?
options: The product may have a memory or instruction feature; check its controls and scope.
The model secretly reads every file on the device.
New chats can never receive information from product features.
questions.answer: The product may have a memory or instruction feature; check its controls and scope.
questions.explanation: A new conversation can still receive saved instructions or memory depending on the product and settings.
questions.misconception: New chat always means no persisted product context.
questions.reviewAction: Find the product's official memory or privacy controls before making a claim.

questions.prompt: Which task most clearly needs verification after an assistant answers?
options: Summarising a current eligibility rule that affects an application.
Brainstorming playful names for a private playlist.
Changing a paragraph from formal to friendly.
questions.answer: Summarising a current eligibility rule that affects an application.
questions.explanation: The rule is current and consequential. Check the responsible authority's live source rather than trusting fluent wording.
questions.misconception: A confident answer is enough evidence for a current consequential fact.
questions.reviewAction: Identify the authority, date and exact claim that must be checked.

records.learningObjective: Given one current AI claim and primary evidence, classify the claim, reconstruct the missing operating workflow, design a bounded test and choose an evidence-based next action.
records.prerequisite: Learner can bring one AI claim she would genuinely like to use; the guided and low-risk practices require no account connection or private data.
records.mentalModel: A feature is one capability. A usable workflow is the complete path from a bounded outcome through authorized inputs, configuration, human judgement, boundaries, tests and upkeep.
adjacentDistinctions: supported as stated versus true but incomplete
one polished output versus tested operating evidence
human review label versus named human decision and checkpoint
misconceptions: If the feature exists, the workflow already exists.
If the demonstration worked once, my setup must be the problem.
Human in the loop is a sufficient control without naming the decision.
Customization means adding more personal data.

modality.narration: Name the viral claim, expose the jump cut and teach the eight Missing Middle passes without mocking the learner or creator.
modality.images: Use fictional generic product interfaces and visible workflow evidence; every image must match the narration at that moment.
modality.animation: Animate the missing operating layers entering between capability and outcome. Do not use decorative motion as a substitute for the workflow.
modality.demonstration: Compare one favorable-output shortcut with normal, edge and stop cases against declared acceptance criteria.
modality.captions: Caption final approved narration verbatim and keep every classification, boundary and decision readable without audio.

analogy.text: A viral AI reel is a makeover montage: it can show the reveal while skipping the fittings, lighting, tailoring and person checking the mirror.
analogy.limit: The analogy explains the jump cut only; it does not imply that AI work is cosmetic, effortless or safe without evidence.

uncertainty: Product access, permissions, plan availability and workflow behavior can change.
A responsible source can establish capability but cannot prove a learner's complete operating setup.

sources.title: Skills in ChatGPT
supports: Skills can package reusable instructions, examples, supporting resources and code.
Access and permissions depend on product, plan and workspace configuration.
Automated scanning does not replace the user's own review, policies or judgement.

sources.title: Plugins in ChatGPT and Codex
supports: Reusable workflow guidance is distinct from apps that connect to external systems and data.
Plugin capabilities inherit underlying app permissions.

records.objective: Check whether the learner can distinguish a feature from a workflow and choose the missing evidence or appropriate next action.

questions.prompt: A current product page confirms that a reusable skill can package instructions and examples. What has that evidence established?
options: The capability exists, but the operating workflow still needs to be designed and tested.
The skill can now own a department's decisions.
Every account has the same access and permissions.
questions.answer: The capability exists, but the operating workflow still needs to be designed and tested.
questions.explanation: A responsible source can establish current capability. It does not prove access, setup, boundaries, accountability or performance for a particular job.
questions.misconception: Feature evidence proves the whole workflow.
questions.reviewAction: Return to the Capability and Prerequisites passes and name what the source does not establish.

questions.prompt: Which statement names a real human checkpoint?
options: Maya verifies every proposed eligibility conclusion against the cited rule before it is sent.
A human stays in the loop.
Someone checks it when necessary.
questions.answer: Maya verifies every proposed eligibility conclusion against the cited rule before it is sent.
questions.explanation: The useful control names the person, decision, evidence and moment of review.
questions.misconception: Human in the loop is specific enough to operate.
questions.reviewAction: Rewrite the control with a named owner, exact decision and visible evidence.

questions.prompt: A workflow succeeds on one clean example. What is the strongest next test?
options: Run a normal case, an edge case and a case that should stop against criteria chosen in advance.
Repeat the same favorable example until it looks consistent.
Use real private data so the test feels realistic.
questions.answer: Run a normal case, an edge case and a case that should stop against criteria chosen in advance.
questions.explanation: A bounded test must reveal expected behavior, ambiguity and refusal or escalation—not just repeat the reveal shot.
questions.misconception: One favorable result is enough operating evidence.
questions.reviewAction: Add an edge case, a stop case and a declared acceptance test to the card.

questions.prompt: The capability is real, but the instructions and stop conditions are incomplete. Which decision fits best?
options: Revise
Build
Pretend the missing parts are implementation details
questions.explanation: Revise preserves the useful capability while refusing to call the incomplete setup ready.
questions.misconception: A real feature always requires either immediate adoption or total rejection.
questions.reviewAction: Name the smallest setup or test change required before another decision.

questions.prompt: What belongs in the Upkeep pass?
options: A named owner, the changes that trigger a re-check and a rollback path.
A promise that the product will never change.
The creator's follower count.
questions.answer: A named owner, the changes that trigger a re-check and a rollback path.
questions.explanation: A workflow remains dependable only if someone knows when to re-check it and how to return to a known state.
questions.misconception: A workflow needs setup once and no maintenance.
questions.reviewAction: Add an owner, trigger and rollback path before calling the workflow complete.
